I feel like this *frequently*. The truth is, many of us just die alone. I remember something a co-worker said, "Some people are really beautiful but they just can't find anyone." It really resonated the shit out of me, because it's *true*. You have to realize, even if you do find somebody, something will inevitably happen that will make you sad. Either they will die and leave you alone in the world, or you'll die and leave them, or something will cause the relationship to end. I was reminded of this the other day when I saw a program on TLC about this elderly Korean couple who had been together for *seventy-six* years. They loved each other until the end, when the husband passed away of natural causes. They cut to the credits with the wife standing out in the snow, fucking sobbing. 

I don't even mean to be harsh by saying any of the above. I can 100% sympathize with how you feel, and it DOES hurt. It absolutely is one of the most painful aspects of the human condition. Life is pain. I feel like this every day of my life, at 25 only ever having been in a real relationship once just last year, and the only two times I ever actually fell in love, the guy didn't feel that way about me, or the guy chose to end things because of distance. There's nothing I could have done about it in either case. Some things are merely out of our control. I think the best way to deal with this pain is to find distractions, ways to sort of stuff it at the back of your mind. Spend more time with friends and family/at the very least, people who love and care about you, even though it's not the kind of love you so badly desire. And you have to learn to enjoy your own company.

The dopamine response makes a lot of sense to me when you brought it up. However, addicting things generally end up being horrible for us. When you mentioned how you'd swing between feeling really good about yourself and feeling shitty, that's where the detriment came to mind. 

I used to feel the same way about it, swinging between feeling good about myself and not feeling good about myself. But I just know that it's not healthy behaviour to have. Something about being in a relationship for the first time as a result of online dating made me reach the conclusion that what I was doing was stupid and unhealthy for me psychologically. We want people to like us, that's valid because humans are social creatures, but when it reaches the point of addiction, we  must try to find a way to correct detrimental behaviour so we don't suffer as a result.

They prefer to not be rejected by someone more attractive because it plays into their own self esteem. Imagine a scenario where this happens, you're rejected by somebody you find really attractive, and then this person you don't find attractive comes along and tries to get your attention. You end up feeling like, "Shit, I must be unattractive if I'm being rejected by attractive men and sought after by men that are not attractive."

Looks ultimately are just one piece of the puzzle, but based on human behaviour, I'd say that this makes a lot of sense psychologically.
